q: What unit area do the DOH guidelines give per person for a waiting area?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 21 and Note 1
n: 0.65 m² per person occupying the space at one time. Remember this: the five "magic numbers" are 0.65 (waiting, per person), 1.40 (conference/dining, per person), 5.02 (per staff desk), 7.43 (per bed), 4.65 (small fixed rooms). Waiting is the tightest because people only sit.

q: What is the DOH work area per staff (one desk, one chair, visitor space, aisle)?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 21 and Note 2
n: 5.02 m²/staff covers a desk, chair, occasional visitor and aisle.

q: What unit area per person applies to a conference room or dining room?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 21 and Note 3
n: Conference and dining: 1.40 m² per person.

q: What minimum area do the DOH guidelines give for a hospital toilet (public, staff or ER)?
n: Toilets are 1.67 m²; locker room with toilet is 2.32 m².

q: What is the minimum area of the hospital pharmacy?
n: Pharmacy: 15.00 m² (listed under admin and again under ancillary service).

q: What is the minimum garage area per the DOH space table?
What unit area does the cadaver holding room use?
n: Cadaver holding is computed like a bed space: 7.43 m² per bed.

q: Most dietary areas (supply receiving, cold and dry storage, food preparation, cooking, serving, washing) have what minimum area each?
n: Dietary work areas: 4.65 m² each; garbage disposal area only 1.67 m².

q: Which dietary space has the smallest listed area?
o: Staff locker room and toilet (2.32 sq. m.)

q: Which needs MORE floor area per occupant: a waiting area or a conference room?
o: Waiting area (0.65 vs 1.40 sq. m. per person)
Conference room (1.40 vs 0.65 sq. m. per person)
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 21, Notes 1 and 3
n: People in a conference room sit at tables; waiting seats are packed tighter.
